1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
     6	the manuscript revision 975feb3, and labels are written exactly as in its
     7	LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
     8	and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98 and 3920258.
     9	The later revisions changed prose, titles, the literature review, layout and
    10	figures, added a zero-covariance remark after `H:homog` and qualified a strict
    11	comparison in `T:first` (not cited here) as asserted only for nonzero
    12	covariance. Every cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at
    13	3920258 and 975feb3. Between these two revisions every cited lemma,
    14	proposition, theorem and equation has the same statement and proof up to
    15	whitespace and braces, with one exception: the statement of `T:full-upper`
    16	(cited only as not formalized) now ends with a cross-reference to Theorem
    17	`T:intro-upper` instead of Goal `G:upper`, and its mathematics is unchanged.
    18	The cited sections `S:model` (the zero-covariance remark and a roadmap
    19	figure), `S:two-clock-screen` (Goal `G:sharp` renamed Theorem
    20	`T:intro-second-moment` in the prose), `S:temporal-equilibrium` and
    21	`S:intrinsic-white-evaluation` (new attribution paragraphs) changed only in
    22	prose. TeX line numbers were moved to 975feb3 by a line map; each cited range
    23	lies in unchanged text (script checks recorded in
    24	`provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).

   925	Formalizes the rest of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`

   927	`E:damped-norm-definitions`, lines 745-755; lemma, lines 766-792, with the

   930	`N_2(theta)^2 >= 0` were already formalized (`DampedNorms`, `ClockCopy`,
   931	re-issued with nothing supplied in `ClockCopyHomog`). This module adds
   932	`N_0(theta) = theta^(-2)`, the scaling identities
   933	`N_1(theta) = theta^(alpha+alpha0-2) N_1(1)` and
   934	`N_2(theta)^2 = theta^(-beta) N_2(1)^2` with `beta = 4-alpha-alpha0`, both

   937	smoothing and truncation sentence. The wrapper
   938	`damped_homogeneous_norms_paper` bundles all of these with the finiteness
   939	part and `N_2(theta)^2 >= 0`. It assumes `H:homog`
   940	(`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, temporal
   941	exponent `a = alpha0`) and NOT `Gamma != 0`, as in the TeX, plus one
   942	supplied input used only by the `N_0` conclusions.

   947	is defined for an arbitrary family `G` of measures on `R^d` and

   953	Reading of the smoothing sentence (Le's decision for wave L5, the default
   954	answer adopted on 2026-11-11). "Spatial Gaussian smoothing" and "Gaussian
   955	smoothing of the Green kernel" are read as a measurable multiplier
   956	`g : R^d -> [0,1]` on the spectral measure: `mu` is replaced by
   957	`g(xi) mu(dxi)` (`smoothed mu g`). Green smoothing `p_eta * G_s` multiplies
   958	`G_s hat(xi) G_t hat(xi)` by `e^(-eta norm(xi)^2)`, which depends on `xi`

   967	measurable `g <= 1`, the first and second norms of `g mu` restricted to `S`
   968	are at most those of `mu` restricted to `S'`; `S' = (0,inf)` gives the full

1594	## MaskedAuxiliaryNorm (whole result)
  1595	
  1596	Formalizes `P:masked-auxiliary-norm` (Auxiliary mask norm) of
  1597	`S:masked-covariance` (`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex` at
  1598	`975feb3`: statement lines 88-100 with the displays
  1599	`E:masked-auxiliary-growth` (lines 90-92) and `E:masked-hilbert-fourier`
  1600	(lines 95-98), proof lines 102-137), together with the setup of lines 79-86
  1601	(`zeta_R`, `k_R`, `L`, and `E:masked-auxiliary-measure` at lines 83-86).
  1602	Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.
  1603	
  1604	Conventions. The section's unitary Fourier transform (lines 8-12),
  1605	`f-hat(xi) = c_d int e^(-i xi.x) f(x) dx` with `c_d = (2 pi)^(-d/2)`, is
  1606	defined directly as `paperHat` (for `f` with values in any complex normed
  1607	space; the integral is a Bochner integral over Lebesgue measure on
  1608	`R^d = EuclideanSpace R (Fin d)`), with `cd` the constant. It is not Mathlib's
  1609	`𝓕` (kernel `e^(-2 pi i <v,w>)`); `paperHat_eq_fourier` relates the two
  1610	(`f-hat(xi) = c_d 𝓕 f(xi/(2 pi))`), and `paper_inversion` is Fourier inversion
  1611	in the paper's convention. For a Schwartz map the defining integrand is
  1612	integrable (`integrable_paperHat_integrand`), so the transforms in the
  1613	statements are not junk values. `zetaR`, `kR` and `Lz` are the manuscript's
  1614	`zeta_R(x) = zeta(x/R)`, `k_R = zeta_R-hat` and `L = norm(zeta-hat)_1`; `zeta`
  1615	is a real Schwartz map (`SchwartzMap (Rd d) R`), and `zeta_R F` is
  1616	`x -> (zeta_R(x) : C) • F(x)`. The density
  1617	`rho_R(eta) = c_d^2 L int norm(k_R(xi-eta)) mu(dxi)` is `rho`, a lower
  1618	(`[0, inf]`-valued) integral of a nonnegative function, which is the
  1619	manuscript's integral without a junk value; `nu` is
  1620	`volume.withDensity rho`. "Radon" is `IsLocallyFiniteMeasure` (as in
  1621	`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`; on `R^d` a locally finite Borel measure is
  1622	Radon), "even" and "tempered" are the package's `IsEven` and `IsTempered`.
  1623	`C_Gamma` is `MaskedSpectralGrowth.CGamma`, built from the Bochner integral
  1624	`M_Gamma = int e^(-norm(x)^2/4) Gamma(dx)`; it is the manuscript's constant
  1625	when `Gamma` is tempered, as under `H:homog` (`MGamma_pos`). In the general
  1626	forms, which do not assume `Gamma` tempered, `CGamma` is that Bochner
  1627	integral as written.
  1628	
  1629	Statements. `masked_auxiliary_norm_paper` assumes the section's standing
  1630	assumptions (lines 5-6) `H:homog` (`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`)
  1631	and `Gamma != 0` (`a = alpha0` plays no role in this proposition), a real
  1632	Schwartz `zeta != 0` (line 79), and a separable complex Hilbert space `H` with
  1633	an `H`-valued Schwartz map `F` (lines 93-94). It proves: `zeta-hat` is
  1634	integrable and `L > 0`; and for every `R > 0`: `k_R` is integrable with
  1635	`norm(k_R)_1 = L`, `nu_R` is even, tempered and locally finite,
  1636	`nu_R(B(y,r)) <= c_d^2 L^2 C_Gamma r^alpha` for open and closed balls, all
  1637	`y` and `r > 0`, with a right side that does not depend on `R`; and
  1638	`E:masked-hilbert-fourier`: `norm((zeta_R F)-hat)^2` is `mu`-integrable,
  1639	`norm(F-hat)^2` is `nu_R`-integrable, the inequality holds both for lower
  1640	integrals and for Bochner integrals, and the right side is finite (proof
  1641	lines 134-135). It uses the `H:homog` fields `mu_radon` (only to make `mu`
  1642	s-finite), `mu_tempered`, `mu_even`, `spectral` and `scaling`; the other
  1643	fields, `Gamma != 0`, the inner product and the separability of `H` are
  1644	carried but unused. The general form `masked_auxiliary_norm` assumes only:
  1645	`mu` s-finite, tempered and even, `IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu`,
  1646	`SpectralHomogeneous Gamma (d - alpha)`, `zeta != 0`, and `E` any complex
  1647	Banach space. The pieces carry their own hypotheses, stated in their rows.
  1648	
  1649	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `mu` s-finite for the Tonelli steps
  1650	(derived from `mu_radon` in the wrapper); integrability of every integrand
  1651	whose Bochner integral is stated; measurability is proved, not assumed; the
  1652	balls are `Metric.ball y r` and `Metric.closedBall y r`.
  1653	
  1654	Proof route (differences from the TeX):
  1655	- `L > 0` (stated without proof at line 82) is proved by Fourier injectivity
  1656	  (`eq_zero_of_paperHat_eq_zero`, from `paper_inversion`).
  1657	- The ball bound follows the TeX: Tonelli and the substitution
  1658	  `u = xi - eta` (`nu_apply`, the display of lines 108-111), then
  1659	  `MaskedSpectralGrowth.closedBall_le` at every center `y + u`
  1660	  (`mu_closedBall_le`) and `norm(k_R)_1 = L`.
  1661	- Radon: local finiteness is derived from the ball bound, not from the
  1662	  continuity of `rho_R` (lines 103-106).
  1663	- Tempered: Peetre's inequality
  1664	  `(1+norm eta)^(-N) <= (1+norm xi)^(-N) (1+norm(xi-eta))^N` and the Schwartz
  1665	  decay of `k_R` give
  1666	  `int (1+norm eta)^(-N) dnu_R <= c_d^2 L (int (1+norm xi)^(-N) dmu)(int (1+norm u)^N norm(k_R(u)) du)`
  1667	  with the exponent `N` of `mu` (`lintegral_weight_nu_le`); this replaces the
  1668	  "same dyadic argument" of lines 113-114.
  1669	- Even: `k_R(-u) = conj k_R(u)` (`zeta` real) and the evenness of `mu`, as in
  1670	  lines 106-107.
  1671	- The convolution identity `(zeta_R F)-hat(xi) = c_d int k_R(xi-eta) F-hat(eta) deta`
  1672	  (lines 116-120) is proved for a Banach-space-valued `F` directly by Fourier
  1673	  inversion of `F` and one Bochner Fubini swap (`paperHat_mask`); the scalar,
  1674	  finite-rank and projection steps of lines 121-127 are not needed.
  1675	- Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz (lines 127-128) is proved from the nonnegativity of
  1676	  `t -> int a (g - t)^2` (`sq_integral_mul_le`); the final Tonelli step
  1677	  (lines 133-134) is `lintegral_nu`.
  1678	
  1679	Narrower than the TeX, or not formalized:
  1680	- The last sentence of the proposition, "For a real `H`, the same assertion
  1681	  holds after complexification" (line 99), is not formalized (Mathlib has no
  1682	  complexification of a real Hilbert space). This is the only part of the
  1683	  statement that is missing.
  1684	- The proof-internal claims that `rho_R(eta)` is finite at every `eta` and
  1685	  that `rho_R` is continuous (lines 103-106) are not formalized; they are not
  1686	  part of the statement, and the Lean route does not need them (`rho` is
  1687	  `[0, inf]`-valued and local finiteness of `nu_R` comes from the ball bound).
  1688	- The wrapper is not instantiated in Lean at a nonzero `Gamma` satisfying all
  1689	  of `H:homog`.
  1690	
  1691	Refutations (`refutations/masked-auxiliary-norm/`):
  1692	- `PeetreFactor`: Peetre's inequality without the factor `(1+norm(xi-eta))^N`
  1693	  is false (`d = 1`, `N = 1`).
  1694	- `CdConvention`: `c_d (2 pi)^d = 1` (the normalization without the square) is
  1695	  false at `d = 2`.
  1696	- `KernelNormScaling`: `norm(k_R)_1 = R^d L` (which would lose the uniformity
  1697	  in `R`) is false for the Gaussian `zeta`, `d = 1`, `R = 2`.
  1698	- `ZetaNonzero`: `L > 0` without `zeta != 0` is false (`zeta = 0`).
  1699	
  1700	The definitions `dil`, `hatS`, `zc` and `zetaS` (the dilation, the transform
  1701	of a Schwartz map as a Schwartz map, and the complex Schwartz forms of `zeta`
  1702	and `zeta_R`) only serve the proof route and have no rows.

  1776	`c_r(t) = cos(rt)` (`cFn`) and `b_r(t) = <r> sin(rt)/r` for `r > 0`,
  1777	`b_0(t) = t` (`bFn`; lines 379-383). `Wave` and `Wave.eval` give the choices

  1784	temporal completion `H_a^C` (lines 297-298). As in
  1785	`MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper`, this norm is modelled
  1786	abstractly. `E` is a complex inner product space. `V` is a submodule of
  1787	`R -> C`, the functions accepted into the completion. `emb : V -> E` is a
  1788	linear inclusion, and `||f||_a` is `||emb f||`. `H_a` is not built in this
  1789	module. The wrapper `masked_continuous_wave_paper` takes the manuscript's
  1790	hypotheses: `0 < a < 1`, `T > 0`, `0 < h <= 1`, `0 <= s`, `s + h <= T`,

  1795	`V`. This is B24's `hmem` quantified over every amplitude B24 accepts. Its
  1796	source is `L:masked-time-completion`, lines 154-155: bounded measurable
  1797	amplitudes on a subinterval, extended by zero, belong to the completion. A
  1798	function that is `C^1` on the compact `I` is bounded there and measurable

2375	## PhaseBessel (whole result)
  2376	
  2377	Formalizes `L:phase-bessel` (Hilbert-valued finite Bessel inequality) of
  2378	`S:wave-variance` (`notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex` at `975feb3`:
  2379	statement lines 346-355 with the display `E:phase-bessel` at lines 350-353,
  2380	proof lines 357-366). The lemma cites no labels, and the section's standing
  2381	assumptions (lines 5-8: `H:homog`, `a = alpha0`, the range of `gamma`) are not
  2382	used by it and are not carried. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The
  2383	general theorem `phase_bessel` holds for any measure space `(X, mu)` (no
  2384	sigma-finiteness), any complete complex inner product space `H` (no
  2385	separability) and any finite index types `iota` (the family index `k`) and

2625	## TimeCompletion (whole result)
  2626	
  2627	Covers two modules, `TimeCompletion` and `MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted`, on
  2628	`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex` at `975feb3`. It formalizes
  2629	`L:masked-time-completion` (lines 141-156, display `E:masked-time-schur` at
  2630	150-152, proof 158-181) with the completion `H_a` constructed. It re-issues
  2631	`L:masked-trig-products` (lines 347-374) and `L:masked-continuous-wave`
  2632	(lines 378-423, display `E:masked-continuous-wave` at 385-389) in this
  2633	concrete `H_a`, with nothing supplied. Standing hypotheses: `T > 0` and
  2634	`0 < a < 1` (the section's `a = alpha0`, lines 4-7). The section also assumes
  2635	`H:homog` and `Gamma != 0`, but lines 5-7 say the purely temporal estimates
  2636	hold independently of `Gamma`. These lemmas are purely temporal, so neither
  2637	hypothesis is assumed.
  2638	
  2639	What is constructed. `L2fun T` is complex `L^2(0,T)` as a space of
  2640	functions (`MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))`). On it,
  2641	`TimeSchur.timeForm` (`<f,g>_a = int int f(t) conj g(s) |t-s|^(-a)`) is a
  2642	Hermitian sesquilinear form (`conj_timeForm`, `timeForm_add_right`,
  2643	`timeForm_smul_right`) and is positive semidefinite (`timeForm_re_nonneg`).
  2644	These are the axioms of a pre-inner product (`core`; the arguments are
  2645	swapped because Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first
  2646	slot). `Ha p` is Mathlib's `UniformSpace.Completion` of the resulting
  2647	pre-Hilbert space `Pre p`, so it is a complex Hilbert space, and functions at
  2648	seminorm distance zero are identified (`coe_eq_of_ae`, the null quotient).
  2649	`emb p` is the inclusion of `L^2(0,T)`. Its squared norm is
  2650	`Re timeForm a T f f` (`emb_norm_sq`). This is faithful to the TeX's "null-quotient completion" for the following reason. The TeX completes the
  2651	real compact smooth tests and then complexifies. `dense_span_realTestSet`
  2652	proves that the complex span of the images of the real tests supported in
  2653	`(0,T)` is dense in `Ha p`. So `Ha p` is the closure of the complexified
  2654	tests, and its norm on a test is the TeX's form. `H_a` is built directly over
  2655	`C`. The TeX's real space is represented by the real functions of
  2656	`emb_norm_sq_real` and the positivity clause, not by a separate real
  2657	Hilbert space.
  2658	
  2659	The paper wrapper `masked_time_completion_paper` has exactly the hypotheses
  2660	`0 < a < 1`, `T > 0` and states, in eight conjuncts:
  2661	- positivity on real compact smooth tests, with integrability of the
  2662	  integrand;
  2663	- separability of `Ha p`;
  2664	- `E:masked-time-schur` for `||emb f||`;
  2665	- the continuous linear extension `extL2 p` on a.e.-classes of
  2666	  `L^2(0,T)`, agreeing with `emb`, with the same constant;
  2667	- the complexification clause: `||emb f||^2` equals the complex double
  2668	  integral with `f(t) conj f(s)`, it is the sum of the squared norms of the
  2669	  real and imaginary parts, and the integrand is integrable;
  2670	- for real `g`, `||emb g||^2` equals the real double integral;
  2671	- interval amplitudes: a bounded a.e.-strongly measurable amplitude on
  2672	  `[c,d]`, extended by zero, lies in `L^2(0,T)` and hence has an image under
  2673	  `emb`;
  2674	- density of the complex span of the real tests' images.
  2675	
  2676	Proof route and differences from the TeX.
  2677	- Positivity follows the TeX (lines 159-172). Gamma subordination
  2678	  (`TimeFractional.rpow_neg_eq_subordination`) and the exponential-kernel
  2679	  identity `exp_abs_eq` give, for `t != s`,
  2680	  `|t-s|^(-a) = int Gamma(a)^(-1) 2 lambda^a 1_(u<=t) e^(-lambda(t-u)) 1_(u<=s) e^(-lambda(s-u)) d lambda du`
  2681	  (`kern_eq_mixture`, an identity in `[0, infinity]`). The TeX argues for each
  2682	  `lambda` separately. Lean makes one Fubini exchange over
  2683	  `[0,T]^2 x (0,infinity) x R` in the general criterion
  2684	  `re_form_nonneg_of_mixture` (s-finite measures, nonnegative measurable
  2685	  weight and profiles). Absolute integrability comes from the Schur bound,
  2686	  as in the TeX (`cross_integrable`). Positivity is proved for every complex
  2687	  `f` in `L^2(0,T)`, which is stronger than the TeX's real tests.
  2688	- Separability uses the separability of `Lp` (Mathlib) and the Lipschitz
  2689	  representative map `ofLp`, not a countable family of tests.
  2690	- The TeX extends the inclusion from tests to `L^2` by density. Here `H_a` is
  2691	  built over `L^2(0,T)`, so the inclusion is defined on all of `L^2`. The
  2692	  density of the tests is proved afterwards by `exists_test_approx`, which
  2693	  uses three ingredients: Mathlib's `MemLp.exist_eLpNorm_sub_le`; a
  2694	  `ContDiffBump` equal to one on `[eta, T-eta]` and supported in
  2695	  `[eta/2, T-eta/2]`; and uniform integrability
  2696	  (`MemLp.eLpNorm_indicator_le`) for the boundary layer.
  2697	- `masked_trig_products_completed_paper` instantiates
  2698	  `MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper` with `E = Ha p`,
  2699	  `V = L2fun T` and `emb p`. `hmem` comes from
  2700	  `MaskedModulation.memLp_modeFn`, and `hnorm` from `emb_norm_sq`.
  2701	- `masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper` instantiates
  2702	  `MaskedContinuousWave.masked_continuous_wave_paper` in the same way. Its
  2703	  `hmem` quantifies over every `A` in `C^1(I)`. For each such `A`,
  2704	  `MaskedModulation.envelope_of_contDiffOn` (using `h > 0`) gives continuity
  2705	  and boundedness on `I`, and `memLp_modeFn` gives membership.
  2706	
  2707	Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
  2708	- `L^2(0,T)` is `MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))`, and `[0,T]` versus
  2709	  `(0,T)` is immaterial.
  2710	- The kernel's diagonal value `0^(-a) = 0` is irrelevant, because the
  2711	  diagonal is null for the product measure (`ae_ne_diag`). The mixture
  2712	  identity is used only off the diagonal.
  2713	- Integrability on `[0,T]^2` is a conjunct of the wrapper's double-integral
  2714	  conclusions (items 1 and 5), so no Bochner integral is Lean's junk `0`.
  2715	- `mixWeight` uses `|lambda|^a`, equal to `lambda^a` on the only values that
  2716	  `mixMeasure` charges, so no `rpow` of a negative base occurs.
  2717	- `M` and `D` in the trig-products wrapper are suprema of bounded nonempty
  2718	  sets (`envelope_of_contDiffOn`).
  2719	
  2720	Hypotheses carried but unused:
  2721	- `tsupport f` in `(0,T)` in item 1 of the paper wrapper (positivity holds on
  2722	  all of `L^2(0,T)`).
  2723	- `h <= 1` in `masked_trig_products_completed_paper`.
  2724

2981	## VariationalMean (whole result)
  2982	
  2983	Formalizes Lemma `L:variational-heat-envelope` (Gaussian envelope for the
  2984	original covariance; `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` at `975feb3`,
  2985	statement lines 23-35, proof 37-62) in full, and the display
  2986	`E:variational-global-mean` of Lemma `L:variational-global-mean` (global
  2987	regularity of the original mean; statement 64-74, proof 76-96), in
  2988	`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalMean.lean`. It reuses the definitions
  2989	of `VariationalDilation`: the convolution `conv` (`(Gamma * phi)(x) = int
  2990	phi(x-y) Gamma(dy)`), the mean `mean` (`h_{Psi,s}`, `E:compact-raw-mean`) and
  2991	the control class `CPos` (`E:variational-positive-class`). The only new
  2992	manuscript object is the heat kernel `heatK eps x = (2 pi eps)^(-d/2)
  2993	e^(-norm(x)^2/(2 eps))` (lines 25-26). Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.
  2994	
  2995	The wrappers state the section's standing assumptions (line 4: a nonzero
  2996	covariance satisfying `H:homog`, with `a = alpha0`) as
  2997	`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu` and `Gamma != 0`;
  2998	the mean is taken with exponent `alpha0`.
  2999	`variational_heat_envelope_paper` (with `eps > 0`) gives, for every `x`, the
  3000	integrability of `y -> p_eps(x-y)` against `Gamma` (so `(Gamma * p_eps)(x)`,
  3001	in particular the value at `0`, is finite), the integrability of the spectral
  3002	integrand against `mu`, the identity of `E:variational-heat-envelope` as
  3003	complex numbers with no normalization factor, `0 <= (Gamma * p_eps)(x) <=
  3004	(Gamma * p_eps)(0)`, and `(Gamma * p_eps)(0) > 0`.
  3005	`variational_global_mean_paper` (with `Psi in CPos`) gives real
  3006	`M, C_Psi >= 0` with `0 <= h_s(x) <= M` and `|h_s(x) - h_t(x)| <= C_Psi
  3007	|s - t|` for `s, t in I = [0,1]` and every `x` (the sup-norm bound of the
  3008	display, stated pointwise in `x`). It also gives the integrability of every
  3009	integrand in the definition of `h_s(x)`, the continuity of `x -> h_s(x)` and
  3010	the integrability of `h_s f^2` for every `f in L^2`.
  3011	`variational_global_mean_lipschitz_paper` adds a joint Lipschitz bound on
  3012	`I x R^d`; the TeX does not state it.
  3013	`isRayleighTrial_mean_iff_paper` shows that the explicit side condition
  3014	`integrable_pot` of `WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial` is automatic for `h_s`,
  3015	`s in [0,1]`.
  3016	
  3017	General forms: `heat_envelope` assumes `Gamma`, `mu` tempered (`IsTempered`)
  3018	and the spectral convention `IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu`, without
  3019	`Gamma != 0`; `heat_conv_pos` assumes `Gamma` tempered and `Gamma != 0`;
  3020	`heat_identity` assumes only the spectral convention; `global_mean` assumes
  3021	`Gamma`, `mu` tempered, the spectral convention, `Psi in CPos` and `a < 1`.
  3022	
  3023	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `eps > 0`. Finiteness of
  3024	`(Gamma * p_eps)(0)` and of `h_s(x)` is stated as integrability of the
  3025	integrands. A Lean Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is `0`, so
  3026	without these conclusions the bounds could hold through that junk value.
  3027	`M` and `C_Psi` are nonnegative real numbers.
  3028	
  3029	Hypotheses carried but unused. The wrappers use the `H:homog` fields
  3030	`Gamma_tempered`, `mu_tempered` and `spectral`; the global-mean wrappers also
  3031	use `alpha0_lt_one`. `Gamma != 0` is used only for the strict positivity in
  3032	`L:variational-heat-envelope`, and the global-mean wrappers carry it unused.
  3033	The other fields (`dim`, `alpha0_pos`, `Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`,
  3034	`Gamma_posdef`, `mu_radon`, `mu_even`, `scaling`, `threshold`, `alpha_range`)
  3035	are carried, unused.
  3036	
  3037	Proof-route differences.
  3038	- The identity of `E:variational-heat-envelope` comes from
  3039	  `MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectral_translated_gauss`: the spectral convention
  3040	  applied to one Gaussian Schwartz test, with Mathlib's Gaussian Fourier
  3041	  integral. The TeX pairs with an arbitrary Schwartz test and uses
  3042	  uniqueness of continuous distributions (lines 48-57).
  3043	- Integrability against `Gamma` and `mu` comes from the package's integral
  3044	  form of temperedness, not from polynomial ball growth (lines 38-44).
  3045	- The bound by the value at `0` follows line 59 but does not use evenness of
  3046	  `mu`: the spectral integral is real because it equals the real left side.
  3047	- For the mean, `|Psi(u,z)| <= C e^(-norm(z)^2/2)` (spatial support) and the
  3048	  envelope at `eps = 1` (`gauss_conv`) bound `Gamma * Psi(u,.)` uniformly, as
  3049	  in lines 78-82 for the underived case.
  3050	- The change of variables `r = s - u` (lines 84-88) is
  3051	  `integral_sub_left_eq_self`. The integral runs over `(-1,1)` rather than
  3052	  `R`, since the integrand vanishes outside `(-1,1)` for `s in [0,1]`. The
  3053	  time constant is `int_(-1)^1 |r|^(-a) dr = 2/(1-a)` (`a < 1`).
  3054	- The Lipschitz bound in time does not differentiate under the integral (the
  3055	  TeX's route, lines 82-94). It applies the Lipschitz bound of the smooth,
  3056	  compactly supported `Psi` (`ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport`)
  3057	  inside both integrals, dominated by the same Gaussian envelope.
  3058	
  3059	Narrower conclusion and not formalized:
  3060	- the first sentence of `L:variational-global-mean`, "every mixed time and
  3061	  space derivative of `h_s` is globally bounded in space, uniformly on
  3062	  compact time intervals" (no derivative of `h_s` is formalized; only the
  3063	  display `E:variational-global-mean` on `I = [0,1]`, plus the spatial and
  3064	  joint Lipschitz bounds, which are first-order statements without
  3065	  derivatives);
  3066	- the smoothness of `x -> (Gamma * p_eps)(x)` mentioned in the proof of
  3067	  `L:variational-heat-envelope` (lines 44-46), which is not part of its
  3068	  statement.
  3069	
  3070	Five refutations in `refutations/variational-mean/` prove that the following
  3071	wrong variants are false:
  3072	- strict positivity of `(Gamma * p_eps)(0)` without `Gamma != 0`
  3073	  (`Gamma = mu = 0`);
  3074	- the identity with an extra factor `(2 pi)^(-d)` (`d = 1`, Lebesgue `Gamma`,
  3075	  `mu = delta_0`);
  3076	- a strict peak `(Gamma * p_eps)(x) < (Gamma * p_eps)(0)` for `x != 0` (same
  3077	  example, where the convolution is constant);
  3078	- integrability of `|r|^(-a)` on `(-1,1)` with `a < 1` relaxed to `a <= 1`;
  3079	- the one-sided constant `1/(1-a)`.

   127	theorem bracket_add_le (x e : ℝ) : bracket (x + e) ≤ (1 + |e|) * bracket x := by
   128	  have h1 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1 + |e| := by positivity
   129	  have hx : 2 * |x| ≤ 1 + x ^ 2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (|x| - 1), sq_abs x]
   130	  have hxe : x * e ≤ |x| * |e| := (le_abs_self _).trans_eq (abs_mul x e)

   132	    rw [mul_pow, bracket, Real.sq_sqrt (by positivity)]
   133	    nlinarith [abs_nonneg e, sq_abs e, mul_nonneg (abs_nonneg e) (sq_nonneg (|x| - 1)),

   120	/-! ### Definitions -/
   121	
   122	/-- The supplied input for `N₀`: the mass identity `G_s(ℝ^d) = s` for `s > 0`
   123	(proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`, line 825), stated for a family `G` of
   124	measures on `ℝ^d` standing for the wave Green measures, which this package
   125	does not define. -/
   126	structure GreenMass (G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)) : Prop where
   127	  mass : ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → G s univ = ENNReal.ofReal s
   128	
   129	/-- `N₀(θ) = ∫_0^∞ e^{-θs} G_s(ℝ^d) ds` (`E:damped-norm-definitions`, line 747),
   130	for a family `G` of measures on `ℝ^d`. -/
   131	def N0 (G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)) (θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   132	  ∫ s in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Real.exp (-(θ * s)) * (G s univ).toReal
   133	
   134	/-- The first norm with the Laplace variable restricted to `S`:
   135	`Γ(a)⁻¹ ∫_{S ∩ (0,∞)} λ^{a-1} R_Γ(θ+λ) dλ`. -/
   136	def N1on (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) : ℝ :=
   137	  (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * ∫ l in S, l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + l) ∂L0
   138	
   139	/-- `N₁^{(M)}(1)`, the first norm at `θ = 1` with `λ > M` (lines 782-784). -/
   140	def N1tail (a M : ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) : ℝ := N1on a 1 (Ioi M) μ
   141	
   142	/-- The temporal kernel with the Laplace variable restricted to `S`:
   143	`K_S(r) = Γ(a)⁻¹ ∫_{S ∩ (0,∞)} e^{-λ|r|} λ^{a-1} dλ`.  At `r = 0` with
   144	`S ∩ (0,∞)` of infinite `λ^{a-1} dλ`-mass the integral diverges and the Lean
   145	value is the junk value `0`; this happens only on the diagonal `s = t`, a
   146	`P2`-null set. -/
   147	def KS (a : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (r : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   148	  (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * ∫ l in S, subKernel a |r| l ∂L0
   149	
   150	/-- `K_M(r) = Γ(a)⁻¹ ∫_M^∞ e^{-λ|r|} λ^{a-1} dλ` (lines 778-781), the
   151	`λ`-integral taken over `(M,∞) ∩ (0,∞)`. -/
   152	def KM (a M r : ℝ) : ℝ := KS a (Ioi M) r

   155	def N2onOuter (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ :=

   157	    ∫ ξ, waveHat p.1 ξ * waveHat p.2 ξ ∂μ

   162	    (waveHat z.1.1 z.2 * waveHat z.1.2 z.2)

   164	/-- The squared second norm with `K_S(s-t)` in place of `|s-t|^{-a}`. -/
   165	def N2onSq (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) : ℝ :=

   198	  refine mul_nonneg (by positivity) (integral_nonneg_of_ae ?_)
   199	  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae ae_L0_pos] with l hl

   204	theorem KS_le (a : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (r : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hr : r ≠ 0) :

   209	  rw [rpow_neg_eq_subordination a |r| ha hr', KS]

   217	  rw [rpow_neg_eq_subordination a |r| ha (abs_pos.2 hr), KS, Measure.restrict_univ]

   222	    Tendsto (fun M : ℝ => ∫ l in Ioi M, f l ∂L0) atTop (𝓝 0) := by

   251	
   252	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route (the abstract form of TeX lines 170-171, "its
   253	quadratic form is an integral of a square"): let `μ` on `ℝ` and `ν` on `W` be
   254	s-finite, `ρ ≥ 0` measurable on `W`, `φ ≥ 0` jointly measurable on `W × ℝ`, and
   255	`K ≥ 0` a kernel with `K(t,s) = ∫ ρ(w) φ_w(t) φ_w(s) dν(w)` (in `[0,∞]`) for
   256	`μ⊗μ`-a.e. `(t,s)`.  If `f` is a.e.-strongly measurable and
   257	`f(t) conj f(s) K(t,s)` is `μ⊗μ`-integrable, then
   258	`Re ∬ f(t) conj f(s) K(t,s) ≥ 0`; indeed the integral equals
   259	`∫ ρ(w) |∫ f φ_w dμ|² dν(w)` (Fubini on the triple product). -/
   260	theorem re_form_nonneg_of_mixture {W : Type*} [MeasurableSpace W]
   261	    (μ : Measure ℝ) [SFinite μ] (ν : Measure W) [SFinite ν]
   262	    (ρ : W → ℝ) (hρ : Measurable ρ) (hρ0 : ∀ w, 0 ≤ ρ w)
   263	    (φ : W → ℝ → ℝ) (hφ : Measurable (Function.uncurry φ)) (hφ0 : ∀ w t, 0 ≤ φ w t)
   264	    (K : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ) (hK0 : ∀ p, 0 ≤ K p)
   265	    (hK : ∀ᵐ p ∂(μ.prod μ),
   266	      ENNReal.ofReal (K p) = ∫⁻ w, ENNReal.ofReal (ρ w * φ w p.1 * φ w p.2) ∂ν)
   267	    (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ)
   268	    (hint : Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => f p.1 * conj (f p.2) * (K p : ℂ)) (μ.prod μ)) :
   269	    0 ≤ (∫ p, f p.1 * conj (f p.2) * (K p : ℂ) ∂(μ.prod μ)).re := by
   270	  set m := μ.prod μ
   271	  set F : (ℝ × ℝ) × W → ℂ := fun q =>
   272	    f q.1.1 * conj (f q.1.2) * ((ρ q.2 * φ q.2 q.1.1 * φ q.2 q.1.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) with hFdef
   273	  have hkm : Measurable fun q : (ℝ × ℝ) × W => ρ q.2 * φ q.2 q.1.1 * φ q.2 q.1.2 := by
   274	    have h1 : Measurable fun q : (ℝ × ℝ) × W => φ q.2 q.1.1 :=
   275	      hφ.comp (measurable_snd.prodMk (measurable_fst.comp measurable_fst))
   276	    have h2 : Measurable fun q : (ℝ × ℝ) × W => φ q.2 q.1.2 :=
   277	      hφ.comp (measurable_snd.prodMk (measurable_snd.comp measurable_fst))
   278	    exact ((hρ.comp measurable_snd).mul h1).mul h2
   279	  have hknn : ∀ q : (ℝ × ℝ) × W, 0 ≤ ρ q.2 * φ q.2 q.1.1 * φ q.2 q.1.2 := fun q =>
   280	    mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg (hρ0 _) (hφ0 _ _)) (hφ0 _ _)
   281	  have hFm : AEStronglyMeasurable F (m.prod ν) := by
   282	    refine ((hf.comp_fst.comp_fst).mul ?_).mul ?_
   283	    · exact (Complex.continuous_conj.comp_aestronglyMeasurable hf.comp_snd).comp_fst
   284	    · exact (Complex.continuous_ofReal.measurable.comp hkm).aestronglyMeasurable
   285	  -- the a.e. section identity
   286	  have hsec : ∀ᵐ p ∂m, ∫ w, F (p, w) ∂ν = f p.1 * conj (f p.2) * (K p : ℂ) := by
   287	    filter_upwards [hK] with p hp
   288	    have hmw : Measurable fun w => ρ w * φ w p.1 * φ w p.2 :=
   289	      hkm.comp (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_id)
   290	    have hKr : ∫ w, ρ w * φ w p.1 * φ w p.2 ∂ν = K p := by
   291	      rw [integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae (ae_of_all _ fun w => hknn (p, w))
   292	        hmw.aestronglyMeasurable, ← hp, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (hK0 p)]
   293	    simp only [hFdef]
   294	    rw [integral_const_mul, integral_complex_ofReal, hKr]
   295	  -- integrability on the triple product
   296	  have hFi : Integrable F (m.prod ν) := by
   297	    refine ⟨hFm, ?_⟩
   298	    have hen : ∀ q : (ℝ × ℝ) × W, ‖F q‖ₑ = ‖f q.1.1‖ₑ * ‖f q.1.2‖ₑ *
   299	        ENNReal.ofReal (ρ q.2 * φ q.2 q.1.1 * φ q.2 q.1.2) := by
   300	      intro q
   301	      simp only [hFdef, enorm_mul, RCLike.enorm_conj]
   302	      rw [← ofReal_norm (((ρ q.2 * φ q.2 q.1.1 * φ q.2 q.1.2 : ℝ) : ℂ)), Complex.norm_real,
   303	        Real.norm_of_nonneg (hknn q)]
   304	    have hm2 : AEMeasurable (fun q : (ℝ × ℝ) × W => ‖F q‖ₑ) (m.prod ν) :=
   305	      hFm.enorm
   306	    show ∫⁻ q, ‖F q‖ₑ ∂(m.prod ν) < ∞
   307	    rw [lintegral_prod _ hm2]
   308	    have heq : ∀ᵐ p ∂m, ∫⁻ w, ‖F (p, w)‖ₑ ∂ν =
   309	        ‖f p.1 * conj (f p.2) * (K p : ℂ)‖ₑ := by
   310	      filter_upwards [hK] with p hp
   311	      simp_rw [hen]
   312	      have hmw : Measurable fun w => ENNReal.ofReal (ρ w * φ w p.1 * φ w p.2) :=
   313	        ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp (hkm.comp (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_id))
   314	      rw [lintegral_const_mul _ hmw, ← hp]
   315	      simp only [enorm_mul, RCLike.enorm_conj]
   316	      rw [← ofReal_norm (K p : ℂ), Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_of_nonneg (hK0 p)]
   317	    rw [lintegral_congr_ae heq]
   318	    exact hint.2
   319	  -- assemble
   320	  have hswap : ∫ p, ∫ w, F (p, w) ∂ν ∂m = ∫ w, ∫ p, F (p, w) ∂m ∂ν :=
   321	    integral_integral_swap (f := fun p w => F (p, w)) hFi
   322	  have hinner : ∀ w, ∫ p, F (p, w) ∂m =
   323	      ((ρ w * Complex.normSq (∫ t, f t * (φ w t : ℂ) ∂μ) : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
   324	    intro w
   325	    have hpt : ∀ p : ℝ × ℝ, F (p, w) = (ρ w : ℂ) * ((f p.1 * (φ w p.1 : ℂ)) *
   326	        conj (f p.2 * (φ w p.2 : ℂ))) := by
   327	      intro p
   328	      simp only [hFdef, map_mul, Complex.conj_ofReal, Complex.ofReal_mul]
   329	      ring
   330	    simp_rw [hpt]
   331	    rw [integral_const_mul]
   332	    erw [integral_prod_mul (μ := μ) (ν := μ) (fun t => f t * (φ w t : ℂ))
   333	      (fun s => conj (f s * (φ w s : ℂ)))]
   334	    rw [integral_conj, Complex.mul_conj]
   335	    push_cast
   336	    ring
   337	  rw [integral_congr_ae (Filter.EventuallyEq.symm hsec), hswap]
   338	  simp_rw [hinner]
   339	  rw [integral_complex_ofReal, Complex.ofReal_re]
   340	  exact integral_nonneg fun w => mul_nonneg (hρ0 w) (Complex.normSq_nonneg _)

   342	/-! ### The form on `L²(0,T)` -/
   343	
   344	/-- `L²(0,T)` as a complex subspace of functions `ℝ → ℂ`: the functions `f` with
   345	`MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))` (`[0,T]` versus `(0,T)` is immaterial).
   346	Its elements are functions, not a.e.-classes; the completion below identifies
   347	functions at seminorm distance zero. -/
   348	def L2fun (T : ℝ) : Submodule ℂ (ℝ → ℂ) where
   349	  carrier := {f | MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))}
   350	  add_mem' := fun hf hg => hf.add hg
   351	  zero_mem' := MemLp.zero
   352	  smul_mem' := fun c _ hf => hf.const_smul c
   353	
   354	/-- Auxiliary: for `f, g ∈ L²(0,T)` and `a < 1`, the integrand
   355	`f(t) conj g(s) |t-s|^{-a}` is integrable on `[0,T]²` (Schur bound applied to
   356	`|f| + |g|`). -/
   357	theorem cross_integrable {a T : ℝ} (ha1 : a < 1) (hT : 0 ≤ T) (f g : ℝ → ℂ)
   358	    (hf : MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))) (hg : MemLp g 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))) :
   359	    Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => f p.1 * conj (g p.2) * ((kern a (p.1 - p.2) : ℝ) : ℂ))
   360	      ((volume.restrict (Icc 0 T)).prod (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))) := by
   361	  set F : ℝ → ℝ := fun t => ‖f t‖ + ‖g t‖
   362	  have hF : MemLp F 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T)) := hf.norm.add hg.norm
   363	  obtain ⟨hi, -⟩ := time_schur_rclike (𝕜 := ℝ) ha1 hT F hF
   364	  refine hi.mono ?_ (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun p => ?_)
   365	  · exact ((hf.aestronglyMeasurable.comp_fst).mul
   366	      (Complex.continuous_conj.comp_aestronglyMeasurable hg.aestronglyMeasurable.comp_snd)).mul
   367	      (Complex.continuous_ofReal.measurable.comp ((measurable_kern a).comp
   368	        (measurable_fst.sub measurable_snd))).aestronglyMeasurable
   369	  · simp only [integrand, F, norm_mul, Complex.norm_conj, Complex.norm_real,
   370	      Real.norm_eq_abs, RCLike.conj_to_real, RCLike.ofReal_real_eq_id, id]
   371	    rw [abs_of_nonneg (kern_nonneg a _)]
   372	    have h1 : 0 ≤ ‖f p.1‖ + ‖g p.1‖ := by positivity
   373	    have h2 : 0 ≤ ‖f p.2‖ + ‖g p.2‖ := by positivity
   374	    rw [abs_of_nonneg h1, abs_of_nonneg h2]
   375	    have hk := kern_nonneg a (p.1 - p.2)
   376	    have e1 : ‖f p.1‖ ≤ ‖f p.1‖ + ‖g p.1‖ := by linarith [norm_nonneg (g p.1)]
   377	    have e2 : ‖g p.2‖ ≤ ‖f p.2‖ + ‖g p.2‖ := by linarith [norm_nonneg (f p.2)]
   378	    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (mul_le_mul e1 e2 (norm_nonneg _) h1) hk
   379	
   380	/-- Auxiliary: for `f, g ∈ L²(0,T)`, `a < 1`, the iterated integral `timeForm` equals the
   381	integral over the product `[0,T]²` (Fubini). -/
   382	theorem timeForm_eq_prod {a T : ℝ} (ha1 : a < 1) (hT : 0 ≤ T) {f g : ℝ → ℂ}
   383	    (hf : MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))) (hg : MemLp g 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))) :
   384	    timeForm a T f g = ∫ p, f p.1 * conj (g p.2) * ((kern a (p.1 - p.2) : ℝ) : ℂ)
   385	      ∂((volume.restrict (Icc 0 T)).prod (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))) := by
   386	  rw [timeForm, integral_prod _ (cross_integrable ha1 hT f g hf hg)]
   387	
   388	/-- The form is additive in its (conjugate-linear) second slot on `L²(0,T)`. -/
   389	theorem timeForm_add_right {a T : ℝ} (ha1 : a < 1) (hT : 0 ≤ T) {f g h : ℝ → ℂ}
   390	    (hf : MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))) (hg : MemLp g 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T)))
   391	    (hh : MemLp h 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))) :
   392	    timeForm a T h (f + g) = timeForm a T h f + timeForm a T h g := by
   393	  rw [timeForm_eq_prod ha1 hT hh (hf.add hg), timeForm_eq_prod ha1 hT hh hf,
   394	    timeForm_eq_prod ha1 hT hh hg, ← integral_add (cross_integrable ha1 hT h f hh hf)
   395	      (cross_integrable ha1 hT h g hh hg)]
   396	  congr 1
   397	  funext p
   398	  simp only [Pi.add_apply, map_add]
   399	  ring
   400	
   401	/-- The form is conjugate-homogeneous in its second slot (no integrability needed). -/
   402	theorem timeForm_smul_right (a T : ℝ) (c : ℂ) (f g : ℝ → ℂ) :
   403	    timeForm a T g (c • f) = conj c * timeForm a T g f := by
   404	  unfold timeForm
   405	  rw [← integral_const_mul]
   406	  congr 1
   407	  funext t
   408	  rw [← integral_const_mul]
   409	  congr 1
   410	  funext s
   411	  simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, map_mul]
   412	  ring
   413	
   414	/-- Hermitian symmetry of the form on `L²(0,T)`: `conj ⟨f,g⟩ = ⟨g,f⟩` (Fubini swap and
   415	the evenness of `|x|^{-a}`). -/
   416	theorem conj_timeForm {a T : ℝ} (ha1 : a < 1) (hT : 0 ≤ T) {f g : ℝ → ℂ}
   417	    (hf : MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))) (hg : MemLp g 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))) :
   418	    conj (timeForm a T f g) = timeForm a T g f := by
   419	  rw [timeForm_eq_prod ha1 hT hf hg, timeForm_eq_prod ha1 hT hg hf, ← integral_conj]
   420	  have h := integral_prod_swap (μ := volume.restrict (Icc (0 : ℝ) T))
   421	    (ν := volume.restrict (Icc (0 : ℝ) T))
   422	    (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => g p.1 * conj (f p.2) * ((kern a (p.1 - p.2) : ℝ) : ℂ))
   423	  rw [← h]
   424	  congr 1
   425	  funext p
   426	  simp only [map_mul, Complex.conj_conj, Complex.conj_ofReal, Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap,
   427	    kern_sub_comm a p.2 p.1]
   428	  ring
   429	
   430	/-- Positive semidefiniteness of the form on all of complex `L²(0,T)` (TeX lines 143-147
   431	assert it on real compact smooth tests; this is stronger): for `0 < a < 1`, `T ≥ 0`
   432	and `f ∈ L²(0,T)`, `Re ∬_{[0,T]²} f(t) conj f(s) |t-s|^{-a} ≥ 0`.  Route as in the
   433	TeX proof (lines 159-172): Gamma subordination and the exponential-kernel identity
   434	(`kern_eq_mixture`) write the kernel, off the null diagonal, as a mixture of products
   435	`φ_w(t) φ_w(s)` with nonnegative weight; Fubini on `[0,T]² × (0,∞) × ℝ`, justified by
   436	the Schur bound, turns the form into `∫ ρ(w) |∫ f φ_w|² ≥ 0`
   437	(`re_form_nonneg_of_mixture`). -/
   438	theorem timeForm_re_nonneg {a T : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hT : 0 ≤ T) {f : ℝ → ℂ}
   439	    (hf : MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))) :
   440	    0 ≤ (timeForm a T f f).re := by

441	  rw [timeForm_eq_prod ha1 hT hf hf]
   442	  refine re_form_nonneg_of_mixture _ mixMeasure (mixWeight a) (measurable_mixWeight a)
   443	    (mixWeight_nonneg a ha0) mixProfile measurable_mixProfile mixProfile_nonneg
   444	    (fun p => kern a (p.1 - p.2)) (fun p => kern_nonneg _ _) ?_ f hf.aestronglyMeasurable
   445	    (cross_integrable ha1 hT f f hf hf)
   446	  filter_upwards [ae_ne_diag T] with p hp
   447	  exact kern_eq_mixture a ha0 p.1 p.2 hp
   448	
   449	/-- The form of real functions is the real double integral:
   450	`⟨g, h⟩_a = ∬ g(t) h(s) |t-s|^{-a}` for `g, h : ℝ → ℝ` (no integrability needed: both
   451	sides are iterated Bochner integrals of the same real integrand). -/
   452	theorem timeForm_ofReal (a T : ℝ) (g h : ℝ → ℝ) :
   453	    timeForm a T (fun t => (g t : ℂ)) (fun t => (h t : ℂ)) =
   454	      ((∫ t in Icc 0 T, ∫ s in Icc 0 T, g t * h s * kern a (t - s) : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
   455	  unfold timeForm
   456	  simp_rw [Complex.conj_ofReal, ← Complex.ofReal_mul, integral_complex_ofReal]
   457	
   458	/-- Auxiliary (calibration, used by the refutations): the form at `f = g = 1` is
   459	`⟨1,1⟩_a = 2T^{2-a}/((1-a)(2-a))` for `a < 1`, `T ≥ 0`. -/
   460	theorem timeForm_one {a T : ℝ} (ha1 : a < 1) (hT : 0 ≤ T) :

   463	  have h := timeForm_ofReal a T (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))

   465	  rw [h]
   466	  congr 1
   467	  simp only [one_mul]
   468	  rw [setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Icc (fun t ht => (integral_row ha1 ht).2),

   471	  have h1 : IntervalIntegrable (fun t : ℝ => t ^ (1 - a)) volume 0 T :=

   477	    (fun x : ℝ => x ^ (1 - a)) T, sub_self, sub_zero,
   478	    integral_rpow (Or.inl hr), Real.zero_rpow (by linarith), sub_zero]

   480	  rw [e]
   481	  have h2a : (2 - a) ≠ 0 := by linarith
   482	  have h1a : (1 - a) ≠ 0 := by linarith
   483	  field_simp
   484	  ring

   501	/-- The pre-Hilbert space: `L²(0,T)` with the (degenerate) inner product
   502	`⟪f, g⟫ = ⟨g, f⟩_a = ∬ g(t) conj f(s) |t-s|^{-a}` (the arguments are swapped because
   503	Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first slot). -/

   506	instance instAddCommGroupPre : AddCommGroup (Pre p) := inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup (L2fun p.T))
   507	instance instModulePre : Module ℂ (Pre p) := inferInstanceAs (Module ℂ (L2fun p.T))

   511	/-- Auxiliary: the function underlying an element of `Pre p`. -/
   512	def Pre.toFun (f : Pre p) : ℝ → ℂ := ((show L2fun p.T from f) : ℝ → ℂ)

   514	/-- Auxiliary: the underlying function is in `L²(0,T)`. -/

   520	/-- The inner-product core of `Pre p`; its positivity is `timeForm_re_nonneg`. -/
   521	@[instance_reducible] def core : PreInnerProductSpace.Core ℂ (Pre p) where
   522	  inner f g := timeForm p.a p.T g.toFun f.toFun
   523	  conj_inner_symm f g := conj_timeForm p.ha1 p.hT.le f.memLp g.memLp
   524	  re_inner_nonneg f := timeForm_re_nonneg p.ha0 p.ha1 p.hT.le f.memLp
   525	  add_left f g h := timeForm_add_right p.ha1 p.hT.le f.memLp g.memLp h.memLp

   538	abbrev Ha := UniformSpace.Completion (Pre p)

   540	/-- The inclusion `L²(0,T) → H_a`, a linear isometry for the seminorm `‖·‖_a`. -/

   542	  (UniformSpace.Completion.toComplₗᵢ (𝕜 := ℂ) (E := Pre p)).toLinearMap

   552	/-- Auxiliary: the inner product of `Pre p` is the form with swapped arguments. -/

    31	  (`IsLocallyFiniteMeasure`, as in `HomogCovariance`);

    33	  `r > 0`, with a bound that does not depend on `R`
    34	  (`E:masked-auxiliary-growth`); and `E:masked-hilbert-fourier`
    35	  `∫ ‖(ζ_R F)^(ξ)‖² μ(dξ) ≤ ∫ ‖F̂(η)‖² ν_R(dη)` with both integrands integrable,
    36	  stated both for Bochner integrals and for lower integrals, together with the
    37	  finiteness of the right side (lines 134-135).  `C_Γ` is
    38	  `MaskedSpectralGrowth.CGamma`.
    39	* The general form `masked_auxiliary_norm` assumes only: `μ` s-finite,
    40	  tempered and even, the spectral convention `IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ`, the
    41	  scaling `Γ(cA) = c^{d-α}Γ(A)` (`SpectralHomogeneous Γ (d - α)`), `ζ ≠ 0`,
    42	  and `E` any complex Banach space (no inner product, no separability).  Its
    43	  constant `C_Γ` involves the Bochner integral `M_Γ`; it is the manuscript's
    44	  constant when `Γ` is tempered (`MaskedSpectralGrowth.MGamma_pos`), as under
    45	  `H:homog`.  The pieces carry their own minimal hypotheses
    46	  (`nu_closedBall_le`, `isTempered_nu`, `isEven_nu`,
    47	  `masked_hilbert_fourier`, ...).

    49	Hypotheses of `H:homog` used by the wrapper: `μ_radon` (only to make `μ`

    51	`Γ ≠ 0`, the inner product and the separability of `H` are carried, unused.

    53	Supplied inputs: none.  The fallback of the wave plan (convolution identity

    56	Narrower than the TeX:
    57	* the last sentence of the proposition, "For a real `H`, the same assertion
    58	  holds after complexification" (line 99), is not formalized (Mathlib has no
    59	  complexification of a real Hilbert space);
    60	* the proof's intermediate claims that `ρ_R` is finite everywhere and
    61	  continuous (lines 103-106) are not formalized: they are not part of the
    62	  statement, and the Lean route proves local finiteness of `ν_R` from the
    63	  ball bound instead.
    64	
    65	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `μ` s-finite for the Tonelli steps
    66	(derived from `μ_radon` in the wrapper); integrability of every integrand
    67	whose Bochner integral is stated; the balls are `Metric.ball y r` and

    70	Proof route (differences from the TeX).
    71	* The transform is related to Mathlib's `𝓕` (kernel `e^{-2πi⟨x,w⟩}`) by
    72	  `paperHat_eq_fourier`; inversion in the paper's convention
    73	  (`paper_inversion`) comes from `Continuous.fourierInv_fourier_eq` and the
    74	  change of variables `w = η/(2π)`; Schwartz properties of `F̂` and `k_R` come
    75	  from `SchwartzMap.fourierTransformCLM` composed with a dilation (`hatS`).
    76	* `L > 0` by Fourier injectivity (the TeX states it without proof).
    77	* Ball bound: Tonelli twice and the substitution `u = ξ - η`, then
    78	  `MaskedSpectralGrowth.closedBall_le` at every center, as in lines 108-113.
    79	* Radon: from the ball bound, not from the continuity of `ρ_R`.
    80	* Tempered: Peetre's inequality
    81	  `(1+|η|)^{-N} ≤ (1+|ξ|)^{-N}(1+|ξ-η|)^N` and the Schwartz decay of `k_R`
    82	  give `∫(1+|η|)^{-N} dν_R ≤ c_d² L (∫(1+|ξ|)^{-N} dμ)(∫(1+|u|)^N|k_R(u)|du)`
    83	  with the exponent `N` of `μ`; this replaces the "same dyadic argument" of
    84	  lines 113-114 and is simpler.
    85	* Even: `k_R(-u) = conj k_R(u)` (`ζ` real) and the evenness of `μ`, as in
    86	  lines 106-107.
    87	* Convolution identity `(ζ_R F)^(ξ) = c_d ∫ k_R(ξ-η) F̂(η) dη` (lines 116-120):
    88	  Fourier inversion of `F` and one Bochner Fubini swap in the Banach space
    89	  directly (`paperHat_mask`); the scalar, finite-rank and projection steps of
    90	  lines 121-127 are not needed.  Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz (lines 127-132) is
    91	  proved by the nonnegativity of the quadratic `t ↦ ∫ a (g - t)²`
    92	  (`sq_integral_mul_le`); the final Tonelli step (lines 133-134) is

   117	/-! ### The unitary Fourier transform of the section -/
   118	
   119	/-- `c_d = (2π)^{-d/2}` (line 11). -/
   120	def cd (d : ℕ) : ℝ := (2 * π) ^ (-(d : ℝ) / 2)
   121	
   122	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   123	theorem cd_pos (d : ℕ) : 0 < cd d := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (by positivity) _
   124	
   125	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. `c_d² (2π)^d = 1`. -/
   126	theorem cd_sq_mul (d : ℕ) : cd d ^ 2 * (2 * π) ^ d = 1 := by
   127	  have h2 : (0 : ℝ) < 2 * π := by positivity
   128	  rw [cd, ← Real.rpow_natCast ((2 * π) ^ (-(d : ℝ) / 2)) 2, ← Real.rpow_mul h2.le,
   129	    ← Real.rpow_natCast (2 * π) d, ← Real.rpow_add h2]
   130	  norm_num
   131	
   132	/-- The unitary Fourier transform of the section (lines 8-12), for a function
   133	with values in a complex normed space `E`:
   134	`f̂(ξ) = c_d ∫ e^{-i ξ·x} f(x) dx`. -/
   135	def paperHat {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] (f : Rd d → E)
   136	    (ξ : Rd d) : E :=
   137	  (cd d : ℂ) • ∫ x, Complex.exp (-(Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) • f x

   141	variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]
   142	
   143	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. The section's transform in terms of
   144	Mathlib's Fourier transform `𝓕 f(w) = ∫ e^{-2πi⟨v,w⟩} f(v) dv`:
   145	`f̂(ξ) = c_d 𝓕 f(ξ/(2π))`. -/
   146	theorem paperHat_eq_fourier (f : Rd d → E) (ξ : Rd d) :
   147	    paperHat f ξ = (cd d : ℂ) • 𝓕 f ((2 * π)⁻¹ • ξ) := by
   148	  rw [paperHat, Real.fourier_eq']
   149	  congr 1
   150	  refine integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_)
   151	  simp only
   152	  congr 2
   153	  rw [real_inner_smul_right, real_inner_comm]
   154	  have hπ : (2 * π) ≠ 0 := by positivity
   155	  push_cast
   156	  field_simp
   157	
   158	/-- The defining integral of the transform converges for a Schwartz map: the
   159	integrand `x ↦ e^{-iξ·x} f(x)` is integrable, so `paperHat` of a Schwartz map
   160	is never a junk value. -/
   161	theorem integrable_paperHat_integrand (f : SchwartzMap (Rd d) E) (ξ : Rd d) :
   162	    Integrable (fun x => Complex.exp (-(Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) • f x) := by
   163	  refine f.integrable.norm.mono' (by fun_prop) (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_)
   164	  rw [norm_smul, Complex.norm_exp]
   165	  simp

   167	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. The dilation `x ↦ c • x` (`c ≠ 0`) as a
   168	continuous linear equivalence. -/
   169	def dil (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) : Rd d ≃L[ℝ] Rd d :=
   170	  (LinearEquiv.smulOfNeZero ℝ (Rd d) c hc).toContinuousLinearEquiv
   171	
   172	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   173	@[simp] theorem dil_apply (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (x : Rd d) : dil c hc x = c • x := rfl
   174	
   175	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. The section's transform of a Schwartz
   176	map, as a Schwartz map. -/
   177	def hatS (f : SchwartzMap (Rd d) E) : SchwartzMap (Rd d) E :=
   178	  (cd d : ℂ) • SchwartzMap.compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℂ
   179	    (dil (2 * π)⁻¹ (by positivity)) (𝓕 f)
   180	
   181	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   182	theorem hatS_apply (f : SchwartzMap (Rd d) E) (ξ : Rd d) : hatS f ξ = paperHat f ξ := by
   183	  rw [paperHat_eq_fourier, hatS, smul_apply,
   184	    SchwartzMap.compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv_apply, Function.comp_apply, dil_apply,
   185	    SchwartzMap.fourier_coe]

   187	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. The transform of a Schwartz map is
   188	continuous. -/
   189	theorem continuous_paperHat (f : SchwartzMap (Rd d) E) : Continuous (paperHat (f : Rd d → E)) := by
   190	  have : paperHat (f : Rd d → E) = hatS f := funext fun ξ => (hatS_apply f ξ).symm
   191	  rw [this]; exact (hatS f).continuous
   192	
   193	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. The transform of a Schwartz map is
   194	integrable. -/
   195	theorem integrable_paperHat (f : SchwartzMap (Rd d) E) : Integrable (paperHat (f : Rd d → E)) := by
   196	  have : paperHat (f : Rd d → E) = hatS f := funext fun ξ => (hatS_apply f ξ).symm
   197	  rw [this]; exact (hatS f).integrable
   198	
   199	/-- Fourier inversion in the section's convention, for a Schwartz map with
   200	values in a complex Banach space: `f(x) = c_d ∫ e^{i η·x} f̂(η) dη` (used in
   201	the proof of `P:masked-auxiliary-norm`, line 121, "Fourier inversion").
   202	Derived from Mathlib's `Continuous.fourierInv_fourier_eq` by the change of
   203	variables `w = η/(2π)`. -/
   204	theorem paper_inversion [CompleteSpace E] (f : SchwartzMap (Rd d) E) (x : Rd d) :
   205	    f x = (cd d : ℂ) • ∫ η, Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ η x : ℝ)) • paperHat f η := by
   206	  have hinv : 𝓕⁻ (𝓕 (f : Rd d → E)) x = f x := by
   207	    have h := f.continuous.fourierInv_fourier_eq f.integrable
   208	      (by rw [← SchwartzMap.fourier_coe]; exact (𝓕 f).integrable)
   209	    rw [h]
   210	  rw [← hinv, Real.fourierInv_eq']
   211	  set g : Rd d → E := fun w => Complex.exp (↑(2 * π * inner ℝ w x) * Complex.I) • 𝓕 (f : Rd d → E) w
   212	    with hg
   213	  have hpt : ∀ η : Rd d, Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ η x : ℝ)) • paperHat f η =
   214	      (cd d : ℂ) • g ((2 * π)⁻¹ • η) := by
   215	    intro η
   216	    rw [paperHat_eq_fourier, hg, smul_comm]
   217	    congr 2
   218	    rw [real_inner_smul_left]
   219	    have hπ : (2 * π) ≠ 0 := by positivity
   220	    push_cast
   221	    field_simp
   222	  simp_rw [hpt]
   223	  rw [integral_smul, Measure.integral_comp_inv_smul_of_nonneg volume g (by positivity),
   224	    finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, smul_smul, ← Complex.coe_smul, smul_smul]
   225	  have hc := cd_sq_mul d
   226	  have : (cd d : ℂ) * (cd d : ℂ) * (((2 * π) ^ d : ℝ) : ℂ) = 1 := by
   227	    rw [← Complex.ofReal_mul, ← Complex.ofReal_mul, ← sq, hc, Complex.ofReal_one]
   228	  rw [this, one_smul]
   229

   232	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. Schwartz maps integrate polynomial
   233	weights: `(1+‖u‖)^N ‖f(u)‖` is integrable. -/
   234	theorem integrable_one_add_pow_mul {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   235	    (f : SchwartzMap (Rd d) E) (N : ℕ) :
   236	    Integrable (fun u : Rd d => (1 + ‖u‖) ^ N * ‖f u‖) := by
   237	  have h0 := f.integrable_pow_mul volume 0
   238	  have hN := f.integrable_pow_mul volume N
   239	  refine ((h0.add hN).const_mul (2 ^ (N - 1))).mono'
   240	    (by fun_prop) (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun u => ?_)

241	  have hb := add_pow_le (zero_le_one' ℝ) (norm_nonneg u) N
   242	  rw [one_pow] at hb
   243	  rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (by positivity)]
   244	  simp only [pow_zero, one_mul]
   245	  calc (1 + ‖u‖) ^ N * ‖f u‖ ≤ 2 ^ (N - 1) * (1 + ‖u‖ ^ N) * ‖f u‖ :=
   246	        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hb (norm_nonneg _)
   247	    _ = 2 ^ (N - 1) * (‖f u‖ + ‖u‖ ^ N * ‖f u‖) := by ring

   251	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. The real Schwartz function `ζ` as a
   252	complex Schwartz map. -/

   262	/-- The kernel `k_R = ζ_R^` (line 80), the section's transform of the mask. -/
   263	def kR (ζ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℝ) (R : ℝ) : Rd d → ℂ :=

   265	
   266	/-- `L = ‖ζ̂‖₁` (line 80). -/

   270	(`R ≠ 0`). -/

   294	/-- The scaling of the kernel (line 81): `k_R(u) = R^d ζ̂(Ru)` for `R > 0`. -/
   295	theorem kR_scale (ζ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℝ) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (u : Rd d) :

   298	  set f : Rd d → ℂ := fun y => Complex.exp (-(Complex.I * (inner ℝ u (R • y) : ℝ))) • (ζ y : ℂ)
   299	    with hf
   300	  have hpt : ∀ x : Rd d, Complex.exp (-(Complex.I * (inner ℝ u x : ℝ))) • (zetaR ζ R x : ℂ) =
   301	      f (R⁻¹ • x) := by
   302	    intro x
   303	    rw [hf]
   304	    simp only [zetaR]
   305	    rw [smul_inv_smul₀ hR.ne']
   306	  simp_rw [hpt]
   307	  rw [Measure.integral_comp_inv_smul_of_nonneg volume f hR.le, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, hf]

   317	    Measure.integral_comp_smul_of_nonneg volume (fun v => ‖paperHat (fun x => (ζ x : ℂ)) v‖) R
   318	      (hR := hR.le), finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, smul_eq_mul, Lz, ← mul_assoc,

   323	theorem eq_zero_of_paperHat_eq_zero (ζ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℝ)

   365	/-- The density `ρ_R(η) = c_d² L ∫ |k_R(ξ-η)| μ(dξ)` of
   366	`E:masked-auxiliary-measure` (line 85), as an `ℝ≥0∞`-valued function (the

   615	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route (weighted Cauchy-Schwarz, lines 127-128, in

   617	integrable, `(∫ a g)² ≤ (∫ a)(∫ a g²)`. -/
   618	theorem sq_integral_mul_le {a g : Rd d → ℝ} (ha : ∀ x, 0 ≤ a x) (hai : Integrable a)
   619	    (hag : Integrable fun x => a x * g x) (hag2 : Integrable fun x => a x * g x ^ 2) :
   620	    (∫ x, a x * g x) ^ 2 ≤ (∫ x, a x) * ∫ x, a x * g x ^ 2 := by
   621	  have hq : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ (∫ x, a x) * (t * t) + (-2 * ∫ x, a x * g x) * t +
   622	      ∫ x, a x * g x ^ 2 := by
   623	    intro t
   624	    have e : (fun x => a x * (g x - t) ^ 2) =
   625	        fun x => (t * t) * a x + (-2 * t) * (a x * g x) + a x * g x ^ 2 := by
   626	      funext x; ring
   627	    have hexp : ∫ x, a x * (g x - t) ^ 2 = (∫ x, a x) * (t * t) +
   628	        (-2 * ∫ x, a x * g x) * t + ∫ x, a x * g x ^ 2 := by
   629	      have i1 : Integrable (fun x => t * t * a x) := hai.const_mul _
   630	      have i2 : Integrable (fun x => -2 * t * (a x * g x)) := hag.const_mul _
   631	      have i12 : Integrable (fun x => t * t * a x + -2 * t * (a x * g x)) := i1.add i2
   632	      rw [e, integral_add i12 hag2, integral_add i1 i2, integral_const_mul, integral_const_mul]
   633	      ring
   634	    rw [← hexp]
   635	    exact integral_nonneg fun x => mul_nonneg (ha x) (sq_nonneg _)
   636	  have hd := discrim_le_zero hq
   637	  rw [discrim] at hd
   638	  nlinarith

1	\section{Covariance bounds for physically masked wave fields}
     2	\label{S:masked-covariance}
     3	
     4	We establish the covariance estimates needed for the operator construction.
     5	Throughout this section, Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} holds, $a = \alpha_0$, and
     6	$\Gamma \ne 0$. For zero spatial covariance, the spatial spectral measures and
     7	noise variances vanish; the purely temporal estimates remain valid independently
     8	of $\Gamma$. We use the unitary Fourier transform
     9	\[
    10	  \widehat{f}(\xi) = c_d\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}f(x)\ud x,
    11	  \qquad c_d = (2\pi)^{-d/2}.
    12	\]
    13	The spectral convention in Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} means that, for every
    14	complex Schwartz test $\varphi$,
    15	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-spectral-convention}
    16	  \int_{\R^d}\varphi(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
    17	  = \int_{\R^d}\left(\int_{\R^d}e^{i\xi\cdot x}
    18	  \varphi(x)\ud x\right)\mu(\ud\xi).
    19	\end{equation}
    20	This is an identity of distribution pairings. We will not interchange two
    21	infinite measures in the associated oscillatory expression.
    22	
    23	A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial mass growth. Indeed, choose a
    24	nonnegative compact smooth test that is at least one on the unit ball, and apply
    25	a defining Schwartz seminorm bound for the distribution to its dilations. Its
    26	mass on a ball of radius $R \ge 1$ is bounded by a power of $R$. Summation over
    27	dyadic shells then gives integrability of $(1+|x|)^{-N}$ for some $N$, and hence
    28	absolute integrability of every Schwartz test. These facts apply to both
    29	$\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Smooth cutoffs converge in the Schwartz topology, so these
    30	integrals agree with the tempered pairings.
    31	
    32	\subsection{Translated spectral growth and physical masks}
    33	
    34	\begin{proposition}[Translated spectral mass]\label{P:masked-spectral-growth}
    35	  Put
    36	  \[
    37	    M_\Gamma = \int_{\R^d}e^{-|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x),
    38	    \qquad C_\Gamma = \frac{eM_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d}.
    39	  \]
    40	  Then $0 < M_\Gamma < \infty$, and for $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$,
    41	  \begin{align}
    42	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    43	    &= \left(\frac{r}{2\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^d
    44	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x),
    45	    \label{E:masked-gaussian-transform}\\
    46	    0 \le \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    47	    &\le \frac{r^\alpha M_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d},
    48	    \qquad \mu(B(y,r)) \le C_\Gamma r^\alpha.
    49	    \label{E:masked-translated-ball}
    50	  \end{align}
    51	  The ball may be open or closed.
    52	\end{proposition}
    53	
    54	\begin{proof}
    55	  Temperedness gives finiteness of $M_\Gamma$. Its positivity follows from
    56	  $\Gamma \ne 0$. To check the Fourier constant, set $J(b) = \int_\R
    57	  e^{-Ax^2}e^{ibx}\ud x$ for $A > 0$. Squaring the real Gaussian integral and
    58	  using polar coordinates gives $J(0) = \sqrt{\pi/A}$. Differentiation and
    59	  integration by parts give $J'(b) = -bJ(b)/(2A)$. Therefore, $J(b) =
    60	  \sqrt{\pi/A}e^{-b^2/(4A)}$. Taking products over the coordinates gives
    61	  \[
    62	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{i(\xi-y)\cdot x}\ud x
    63	    = \left(\frac{2\sqrt{\pi}}r\right)^d e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}.
    64	  \]
    65	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single Schwartz test
    66	  $e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}$ to obtain \eqref{E:masked-gaussian-transform}.
    67	  Its left side is nonnegative. Taking the absolute value on the right removes
    68	  the complex phase because $\Gamma$ is nonnegative. The pushforward of $\Gamma$
    69	  by $x \mapsto rx$ assigns mass $r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$ to a Borel set $A$.
    70	  Thus,
    71	  \[
    72	    \int e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x) = r^{\alpha-d}M_\Gamma.
    73	  \]
    74	  This proves the Gaussian bound. On either ball $B(y,r)$ the integrand
    75	  $e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}$ is at least $e^{-1}$, proving the mass bound. This proves
    76	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth}.
    77	\end{proof}
    78	
    79	Choose and fix a real nonzero Schwartz function $\zeta$. For $R > 0$ put
    80	$\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$, $k_R = \widehat{\zeta_R}$ and $L =
    81	\|\widehat{\zeta}\|_1$. Then $k_R(u) = R^d\widehat{\zeta}(Ru)$ and $\|k_R\|_1 =
    82	L > 0$. Define
    83	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-measure}
    84	  \nu_R(\ud\eta) = \rho_R(\eta)\ud\eta,
    85	  \qquad \rho_R(\eta) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\mu(\ud\xi).
    86	\end{equation}
    87	
    88	\begin{proposition}[Auxiliary mask norm]\label{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}
    89	  The measure $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, with
    90	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}
    91	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) \le c_d^2L^2C_\Gamma r^\alpha
    92	  \end{equation}
    93	  for all $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$, uniformly in $R > 0$. If $H$ is a separable
    94	  complex Hilbert space and $F$ is an $H$-valued Schwartz function, then
    95	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}
    96	    \int \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2\mu(\ud\xi)
    97	    \le \int \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
    98	  \end{equation}
    99	  For a real $H$, the same assertion holds after complexification.
   100	\end{proposition}
   101	
   102	\begin{proof}
   103	  Schwartz decay of $k_R$ and polynomial growth of $\mu$ show that
   104	  $\rho_R(\eta)$ is finite at every $\eta$. On compact sets of $\eta$, the
   105	  integrands have a common integrable bound. Dominated convergence therefore
   106	  makes $\rho_R$ continuous, and $\nu_R$ is Radon. Since $\zeta$ is real,
   107	  $k_R(-u) = \overline{k_R(u)}$. Evenness of $\mu$ gives evenness of $\rho_R$.
   108	  Tonelli's theorem gives
   109	  \[
   110	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(u)|\mu(B(y+u,r))\ud u.
   111	  \]
   112	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth} and $\|k_R\|_1 = L$ give
   113	  \eqref{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}. Polynomial growth on centered balls proves
   114	  temperedness by the same dyadic argument as above.
   115	
   116	  Bochner Fourier integration gives
   117	  \[
   118	    \widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)
   119	    = c_d\int k_R(\xi-\eta)\widehat{F}(\eta)\ud\eta.
   120	  \]
   121	  For scalar Schwartz functions this follows by Fourier inversion and absolute
   122	  integrability. It follows next for finite-rank Hilbert-valued functions. For
   123	  general $F$, take projections onto the successive spans of a countable
   124	  orthonormal basis of its separable range closure. They converge pointwise in
   125	  norm. The Schwartz bounds on $F$ dominate the Fourier integrals, proving the
   126	  identity by dominated convergence. In a finite-dimensional space the full
   127	  identity projection suffices; the zero space is immediate. The triangle
   128	  inequality and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz yield
   129	  \[
   130	    \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2
   131	    \le c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\ud\eta.
   132	  \]
   133	  Integrating against $\mu$ and applying Tonelli's theorem proves
   134	  \eqref{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}. Its right side is finite by Schwartz decay
   135	  and temperedness of $\nu_R$. This proves
   136	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}.
   137	\end{proof}
   138	
   139	\subsection{Temporal completion and the original noise}
   140	
   141	\begin{lemma}[Temporal covariance completion]\label{L:masked-time-completion}
   142	  Let $T > 0$. The form
   143	  \[
   144	    \langle f,g\rangle_a
   145	    = \int_0^T\int_0^T f(t)g(s)|t-s|^{-a}\ud t\ud s
   146	  \]
   147	  is positive semidefinite on real compact smooth tests. Its null-quotient
   148	  completion $H_a$ is separable. The inclusion of tests extends continuously
   149	  from $L^2(0,T)$, with
   150	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-time-schur}
   151	    \|f\|_a^2 \le \frac{2T^{1-a}}{1-a}\|f\|_2^2.
   152	  \end{equation}
   153	  In its complexification the norm is given by the same double integral with
   154	  $f(t)\overline{f(s)}$. In particular, bounded measurable amplitudes on a
   155	  subinterval, extended by zero, belong to this completion.
   156	\end{lemma}
   157	
   158	\begin{proof}
   159	  Write $\Gamma_E$ for Euler's Gamma function. Away from the null diagonal,
   160	  \[
   161	    |t-s|^{-a} = \frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}\int_0^\infty
   162	    \lambda^{a-1}e^{-\lambda|t-s|}\ud\lambda.
   163	  \]
   164	  This follows by substitution in the defining Gamma integral. Moreover,
   165	  \[
   166	    e^{-\lambda|t-s|}
   167	    = \int_{-\infty}^{\min(t,s)}2\lambda
   168	    e^{-\lambda(t-u)}e^{-\lambda(s-u)}\ud u.
   169	  \]
   170	  For each $\lambda > 0$ its quadratic form is an integral of a square. All
   171	  exchanges for compact smooth tests are absolutely integrable because the
   172	  kernel row integral is at most $2T^{1-a}/(1-a)$. The same bound and $2|xy| \le
   173	  |x|^2+|y|^2$ prove~\eqref{E:masked-time-schur}. A countable $L^2$-dense family
   174	  of compact smooth tests is consequently dense in $H_a$, proving separability.
   175	  The complex quadratic form is the sum of those of the real and imaginary
   176	  parts, since symmetry cancels the imaginary cross term. Thus, the same bound
   177	  holds after complexification. Smooth density in $L^2$, together with the Schur
   178	  bound on the absolute bilinear form, extends the inclusion and the integral
   179	  identity to $L^2$. This includes the stated interval amplitudes. This proves
   180	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion}.
   181	\end{proof}
   182	
   183	Let $\mathcal{D}$ consist of finite sums $F(t,x) = \sum_j\tau_j(t)f_j(x)$ with
   184	real $\tau_j \in C_c^\infty(0,T)$ and real Schwartz $f_j$. These give
   185	$H_a$-valued Schwartz functions of $x$. Let $W$ denote the original real
   186	isonormal noise in~\eqref{E:cov}.
   187	
   188	\begin{proposition}[Completion on the same noise]\label{P:masked-noise-completion}
   189	  The space $\mathcal{D}$ belongs to the original test-noise completion and
   190	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-actual-noise-norm}
   191	    \E W(F)^2 = (2\pi)^d\int
   192	    \|\widehat{F}(\xi)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\mu(\ud\xi).
   193	  \end{equation}
   194	  Define the auxiliary seminorm
   195	  \[
   196	    N_R(F)^2 = (2\pi)^d\int
   197	    \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
   198	  \]
   199	  Then $F \mapsto W(\zeta_RF)$ extends as a contraction from the null-quotient
   200	  completion for $N_R$ into the original $L^2(\Omega)$. The extension is
   201	  centered and jointly Gaussian. For finitely many real $F_1,\ldots,F_m \in
   202	  \mathcal{D}$, their masked covariance matrix is bounded in positive
   203	  semidefinite order by the matrix of auxiliary inner products. This gives
   204	  covariance comparison for every finite linear Gaussian image and every convex
   205	  norm power $p \ge 1$.
   206	\end{proposition}
   207	
   208	\begin{proof}
   209	  For real spatial Schwartz $f,g$, put $h(z) = \int f(y+z)g(y)\ud y$. Fourier
   210	  inversion and Parseval give
   211	  \[
   212	    h(z) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}\widehat{f}(\xi)
   213	    \overline{\widehat{g}(\xi)}\ud\xi.
   214	  \]
   215	  Therefore,

216	  \[
   217	    \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}h(z)\ud z
   218	    = (2\pi)^d\widehat{f}(-\xi)\overline{\widehat{g}(-\xi)}.
   219	  \]
   220	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single test $h$ and reflect
   221	  $\xi$ using evenness of $\mu$. The spatial covariance is thus
   222	  $(2\pi)^d\int\widehat{f}(\xi)\overline{\widehat{g}(\xi)}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Summing
   223	  over the finitely many temporal factors gives
   224	  \eqref{E:masked-actual-noise-norm}. Schwartz decay, temperedness and temporal
   225	  integrability justify these pairings. If $W$ is initially given only on
   226	  compact spatial tests, smooth expanding cutoffs converge in the Schwartz
   227	  topology. The spectral form is continuous in that topology, admitting
   228	  $\mathcal{D}$ in the same completion.
   229	
   230	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}, applied with $H =
   231	  H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$, gives $\E W(\zeta_RF)^2 \le N_R(F)^2$. It annihilates
   232	  auxiliary-null tests. An auxiliary Cauchy sequence thus gives a Cauchy
   233	  sequence of noise evaluations in $L^2(\Omega)$, proving the contraction
   234	  extension and its uniqueness. Every finite linear combination of the limits is
   235	  an $L^2$ limit of centered Gaussian variables. Their variances converge, so
   236	  their characteristic functions prove that the limits remain jointly centered
   237	  Gaussian.
   238	
   239	  For the finite family let $A$ be the covariance matrix and $B$ the auxiliary
   240	  Gram matrix. Applying the norm inequality to $\sum_i b_iF_i$ gives
   241	  $b^{\mathsf{T}}Ab \le b^{\mathsf{T}}Bb$ for every real vector $b$.
   242	  Diagonalizing $B-A$ constructs a centered Gaussian vector $Z$ of that
   243	  covariance, independent of the evaluation vector $X$, on a product space. Then
   244	  $X+Z$ has covariance $B$. Conditional Jensen gives $\E\|X\|^p \le \E\|X+Z\|^p$
   245	  for every norm and $p \ge 1$. Finite Gaussian moments ensure finiteness of
   246	  both sides. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:masked-noise-completion}.
   247	\end{proof}
   248	
   249	The auxiliary completion depends on $R$ and $\zeta$. Its construction does not
   250	define multiplication by $\zeta_R$ on the original noise quotient. Nor does the
   251	finite linear Gaussian comparison assert a covariance comparison for nonlinear
   252	wave solutions. The auxiliary and original test norms need not dominate one
   253	another. No spatial representative for every auxiliary class, nonnegative
   254	physical inverse covariance for $\nu_R$, or uniform density bound in $R$ is
   255	asserted.
   256	
   257	\begin{proposition}[A physical mask need not preserve noise-null tests]
   258	  \label{P:masked-quotient-obstruction}
   259	  In the admissible case $d = 2$, $\alpha = 1$, $0 < a < 1$ and $\Gamma =
   260	  \delta_0(\ud x_1)\ud x_2$, there is a real compact smooth mask $\zeta$ such
   261	  that no finite $C$ satisfies $\E W(\zeta F)^2 \le C\E W(F)^2$ for every
   262	  compact smooth test $F$.
   263	\end{proposition}
   264	
   265	\begin{proof}
   266	  Fourier inversion on Schwartz tests gives $\mu =
   267	  (2\pi)^{-1}\ud\xi_1\delta_0(\ud\xi_2)$ in the stated spectral convention. The
   268	  measure $\Gamma$ is nonnegative, even, positive definite and tempered, with
   269	  $\Gamma(cA) = c\Gamma(A)$. It therefore satisfies Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}
   270	  with $\alpha = 1$. This is not spatial white noise in dimension two. For real
   271	  compact smooth $g$, its spatial covariance is, by ordinary Fubini,
   272	  \[
   273	    V(g) = \int_\R\left(\int_\R g(x_1,x_2)\ud x_2\right)^2\ud x_1.
   274	  \]
   275	  Choose real even $\chi \in C_c^\infty(\R)$ equal to one on $[-1,1]$ and zero
   276	  outside $[-2,2]$. For example, on $1 < r = |x| < 2$ use
   277	  \[
   278	    \chi(x) = \frac{e^{-1/(2-r)}}{e^{-1/(2-r)}+e^{-1/(r-1)}}.
   279	  \]
   280	  The endpoint exponentials vanish to every order, so the plateau pastes
   281	  smoothly. Let $I_\chi = \int(\chi')^2 > 0$ and $J_\chi = \int\chi^4 > 0$.
   282	  Positivity of $I_\chi$ follows because $\chi$ is not constant, and $J_\chi \ge
   283	  2$. Put $g(x) = \chi(x_1)\chi''(x_2)$ and $\zeta(x) = \chi(x_1)\chi(x_2)$.
   284	  Their unmasked marginal vanishes since $\int\chi'' = 0$, whereas integration
   285	  by parts gives the masked marginal $-I_\chi\chi(x_1)^2$. Thus, $V(g) = 0$ and
   286	  $V(\zeta g) = J_\chi I_\chi^2 > 0$. For a nonzero nonnegative $\tau \in
   287	  C_c^\infty(0,T)$, set $F(t,x) = \tau(t)g(x)$. The temporal factor
   288	  $\|\tau\|_a^2$ is finite and strictly positive because its nonnegative
   289	  integrand is positive on a set of positive two-dimensional measure.
   290	  Consequently, the full unmasked variance is zero and the masked variance is
   291	  positive. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:masked-quotient-obstruction}.
   292	\end{proof}

   294	\subsection{Temporal modulation and continuous wave factors}
   295	
   296	Write $\langle x\rangle = \sqrt{1+x^2}$. Let $I = [s,s+h] \subset [0,T]$, with
   297	$0 < h \le 1$. Norms below are those of the complexified temporal completion in
   298	Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion}.
   299	
   300	\begin{lemma}[Modulated amplitudes]\label{L:masked-temporal-modulation}
   301	  Let $A \in C^1(I;\mathbb{C})$, $M = \sup_I|A|$ and $D = \sup_I|A'|$. For every
   302	  real $\omega$,
   303	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-temporal-modulation}
   304	    \|1_IA(t)e^{i\omega t}\|_a^2
   305	    \le C_0(a)h^{2-a}(M+hD)^2\langle h\omega\rangle^{a-1},
   306	    \qquad C_0(a) = \frac{16}{1-a}.
   307	  \end{equation}
   308	  The bound is uniform in $T,s,h,A$ and $\omega$.
   309	\end{lemma}
   310	
   311	\begin{proof}
   312	  Put $c(v) = \int_s^{s+h-v}A(u+v)\overline{A(u)}\ud u$ for $0 \le v \le h$.
   313	  Differentiation at the moving endpoint gives
   314	  \[
   315	    c'(v) = -A(s+h)\overline{A(s+h-v)}
   316	    +\int_s^{s+h-v}A'(u+v)\overline{A(u)}\ud u.
   317	  \]
   318	  Thus, $c(h) = 0$, $|c(v)| \le hM^2$ and $|c'(v)| \le M^2+hMD$. Splitting the
   319	  covariance square into its two conjugate triangles gives
   320	  \[
   321	    \|1_IA(t)e^{i\omega t}\|_a^2
   322	    = 2\operatorname{Re}\int_0^h v^{-a}e^{i\omega v}c(v)\ud v
   323	    = 2h^{2-a}\operatorname{Re}\int_0^1 y^{-a}e^{i\omega hy}f(y)\ud y,
   324	  \]
   325	  where $f(y) = c(hy)/h$. Set $K = M+hD$. Then $f(1) = 0$ and $|f|,|f'| \le
   326	  K^2$. If $K = 0$ the assertion is immediate. If $|\omega h| \le 1$, the last
   327	  integral is at most $K^2/(1-a)$ in absolute value, and $\langle\omega
   328	  h\rangle^{a-1} \ge 2^{(a-1)/2}$. The claimed constant is sufficient in this
   329	  case.
   330	
   331	  Now suppose $k = |\omega h| > 1$. On $[0,1/k]$ the integral is at most
   332	  $K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. On $[1/k,1]$, integrate the exponential by parts. The
   333	  endpoint at one vanishes, while the other endpoint contributes at most
   334	  $K^2k^{a-1}$. The derivative integral, divided by $k$, is bounded by
   335	  \[
   336	    \frac{K^2}k\left(a\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a-1}\ud y
   337	    +\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a}\ud y\right)
   338	    \le K^2 k^{a-1}\left(1+\frac1{1-a}\right).
   339	  \]
   340	  Here $k^{-1} \le k^{a-1}$ since $a > 0$. The total is at most
   341	  $4K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. Finally, $k^{a-1} \le \sqrt{2}\langle\omega
   342	  h\rangle^{a-1}$ and $8\sqrt{2} \le 16$. Including the factor $2h^{2-a}$ proves
   343	  the bound for either sign of $\omega$. This proves
   344	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation}.
   345	\end{proof}
   346	
   347	\begin{lemma}[Correlated trigonometric products]\label{L:masked-trig-products}
   348	  Let $r,\rho \ge 0$. Let $P_r$ be either $\cos(rt)$ or $\sin(rt)$, and let
   349	  $Q_\rho$ be either $\cos(\rho t)$ or $\sin(\rho t)$. With the amplitude and
   350	  constant above,
   351	  \begin{align}
   352	    \|1_IAP_rQ_\rho\|_a^2
   353	    &\le C_0(a)h^{2-a}(M+hD)^2\mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho),
   354	    \label{E:masked-trig-products}\\
   355	    \mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho)
   356	    &:= \langle h(r-\rho)\rangle^{a-1}
   357	    +\langle h(r+\rho)\rangle^{a-1}.
   358	    \label{E:masked-frequency-pair}
   359	  \end{align}
   360	\end{lemma}
   361	
   362	\begin{proof}
   363	  Expanding the two trigonometric factors gives four complex exponential modes
   364	  with frequencies $\sigma r+\tau\rho$, $\sigma,\tau \in \{-1,1\}$, and
   365	  coefficients of absolute value $1/4$. In a Hilbert space,
   366	  \[
   367	    \left\|\sum_j c_jv_j\right\|^2
   368	    \le \left(\sum_j|c_j|\right)\sum_j|c_j|\|v_j\|^2.
   369	  \]
   370	  The first coefficient sum is one. Apply
   371	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation} to each mode. Two frequencies have
   372	  absolute value $|r-\rho|$ and two have absolute value $r+\rho$. This gives one
   373	  half of the asserted right side, and hence the bound. Repeated or zero
   374	  frequencies are permitted; no orthogonality or independence of the modes is
   375	  used. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products}.
   376	\end{proof}
   377	
   378	\begin{lemma}[Continuous sine factors]\label{L:masked-continuous-wave}
   379	  Define $c_r(t) = \cos(rt)$ and
   380	  \[
   381	    b_r(t) = \langle r\rangle\frac{\sin(rt)}r\quad(r > 0),
   382	    \qquad b_0(t) = t.
   383	  \]
   384	  For $F_r \in \{c_r,b_r\}$ and $G_\rho \in \{c_\rho,b_\rho\}$,
   385	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-continuous-wave}
   386	    \|1_IF_rG_\rho\|_a^2
   387	    \le C_1(a)(1+T)^4h^{2-a}\mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho),
   388	    \qquad C_1(a) = 4\cdot3^{1-a}C_0(a).
   389	  \end{equation}
   390	\end{lemma}
   391	
   392	\begin{proof}
   393	  For $r \ge 1$, $b_r$ is a sine times a coefficient at most $\sqrt{2}$. For $0
   394	  \le r \le 1$, the fundamental theorem of calculus gives
   395	  \[
   396	    b_r(t) = t\langle r\rangle\int_0^1\cos(vrt)\ud v.
   397	  \]
   398	  This includes $r = 0$. Hence, a product $F_rG_\rho$ is a scalar coefficient of
   399	  absolute value at most two times a normalized integral of
   400	  $t^jP_{r'}(t)Q_{\rho'}(t)$, where $j \in \{0,1,2\}$ and $|r'-r|,|\rho'-\rho|
   401	  \le 1$. The integral is over zero, one or two copies of $[0,1]$; with no
   402	  averages, use a one-point probability space. Its parameter dependence is
   403	  continuous in $L^2(0,T)$ by dominated convergence.
   404	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion} makes it continuous in $H_a$ as well.
   405	  Thus, the averages are Bochner integrals, and their $H_a$ images agree with
   406	  the pointwise averages by continuity of the inclusion. Hilbert Jensen bounds
   407	  the squared norm of an average by the average of the squared norms.
   408	
   409	  Apply Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products} to each integrand with $A(t) = t^j$.
   410	  For $j = 0,1,2$, respectively, $M+hD$ is at most $1$, $T+1$ and $T^2+2T$. In
   411	  every case $(M+hD)^2 \le (1+T)^4$. For real $x,e$, the triangle inequality and
   412	  its reverse imply
   413	  \[
   414	    \frac{\langle x\rangle}{1+|e|}
   415	    \le \langle x+e\rangle \le (1+|e|)\langle x\rangle.
   416	  \]
   417	  The changes in $h(r\pm\rho)$ have magnitude at most two, since $h \le 1$.
   418	  Because $a-1 < 0$, each altered bracket to the power $a-1$ is at most
   419	  $3^{1-a}$ times the original one. Apply these comparisons, Hilbert Jensen and
   420	  the squared scalar coefficient bound four to obtain
   421	  \eqref{E:masked-continuous-wave}. This proves
   422	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave}.
   423	\end{proof}
